title: The coefficient-degree comparison respects the ideal tensor pairing
statement: Let $j:Z\to X$ be any morphism of schemes, let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module, and let $n,e\geq0$ [lem-sc-square-zero-ideal-tensor-unit]. Put $J=\ker(j)$, $P=\mathrm{tensorPullback}(j)$, $F=P(J\otimes L^n)$, $N=(PL)^n$, $a=n(e+1)$, $b=n(0+1)$, $c=n((e+1)+1)$. Define $m:L^a\otimes(J\otimes L^b)\to J\otimes L^c$ by reassociating, braiding $L^a$ past $J$, reassociating back, applying $J\otimes(\mathrm{tensorPowAddIso}_{a,b})^{-1}$ and the arithmetic identification $a+b=c$. For every open $V$ in $Z$, $q\in\Gamma(V,PL^a)$ and $s\in\Gamma(V,P(J\otimes L^b))$, applying boundaryCoefficientDegreeIso at e+1 to $P(m)((\mathrm{boundaryPullbackTensorIso}_{L^a,J\otimes L^b})^{-1}(q\otimes s))$ gives $\rho_F(\mathrm{boundaryCoefficientDegreeIso}_0(s))\otimes\mathrm{boundarySectionDegreeIso}_e(q)$. This concerns only tensor identifications, with no kernel map, lift or square-zero hypothesis.

proof.text: Work locally on an open of X trivializing L and then on its inverse image in Z. Write ell for the generator and ellbar for its pullback. For arbitrary coefficient module J, the trivialization identifies P(J tensor L^d) with PJ tensor the d-fold generator, so any local s is r tensor ellbar^b with r a section of PJ. Write q=h ellbar^a. A trivialization is a sheaf module isomorphism, so this representation is valid for arbitrary sections, without claiming that all tensor sheaf sections globally are pure tensors.

By induction on d, boundaryPullbackPowIso carries the pullback generator to ellbar^d: at zero this is the unit comparison, and at successor the tensor comparison followed by the induction hypothesis. Induction in tensorPowMulIso groups these d copies into blocks of n; tensorPowAddIso joins the two indicated blocks. Thus boundaryIdealTensorProduct sends q tensor s to hr tensor ellbar^(a+b), with the ideal coefficient moved left by the braiding.

Expand boundaryCoefficientDegreeIso. Its initial tensorPowMulIso groups n(e+2) copies into e+2 blocks, and its associator puts the first n copies next to r. Its pullback tensorator and final power comparisons leave that coefficient fixed. The output is hr ellbar^n tensor (ellbar^n)^(e+1). At source degree zero, the same formula gives r ellbar^n tensor 1; the right unitor removes 1. boundarySectionDegreeIso gives h(ellbar^n)^(e+1). Their tensor product is the preceding output. The possible exchange of the L blocks fixes their generator tensors, so it introduces no scalar or sign.

All equalities commute with restriction and hence glue by sheaf separation on the inverse images of the trivializing cover. At n=0 the same calculation is the unit case, with r unchanged and h acting on r; e=0 is the two-block case. Empty opens, zero coefficients and zero q or s give zero on both sides.

lean.statement:
theorem boundaryCoefficientDegreeIso_tensor_product {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (j : Z ⟶ X)
    (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (n e : ℕ) (V : Z.Opens)
    (q : Γ((tensorPullback j).obj (L.tensorPow (n * (e + 1))), V))
    (s : Γ((tensorPullback j).obj (j.ker.toModules ⊗ L.tensorPow (n * (0 + 1))), V)) :
    let a := n * (e + 1)
    let b := n * (0 + 1)
    let c := n * ((e + 1) + 1)
    let m := boundaryIdealTensorProduct j.ker.toModules L a b ≫
      j.ker.toModules ◁ (eqToHom (by
        dsimp [a, b, c]
        congr 1
        simp only [Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_one]) : L.tensorPow (a + b) ⟶ L.tensorPow c)
    (boundaryCoefficientDegreeIso j L n (e + 1)).hom.app V
        (((tensorPullback j).map m).app V
          ((boundaryPullbackTensorIso j (L.tensorPow a)
            (j.ker.toModules ⊗ L.tensorPow b)).inv.app V (tmulSection q s))) =
      tmulSection
        ((ρ_ ((tensorPullback j).obj (j.ker.toModules ⊗ L.tensorPow n))).hom.app V
          ((boundaryCoefficientDegreeIso j L n 0).hom.app V s))
        ((boundarySectionDegreeIso j L n e).hom.app V q)
